target_customer: Teenagers in India and their parents, with revenue from card interchange and fees
problem: Indian teens had no independent banking product. Akudo offered a prepaid card and UPI based account with parental oversight, savings tools and gamified financial learning, called learning first banking.
business_model: Consumer fintech earning card interchange and partner fees via a PPI issuer

founders.name: Sajal Khanna
founders.background_notes: Credit analytics and data science in auto finance at Capital One per the YC page. A press article describes the founders as IIT Roorkee and BITS Pilani alumni, not attributed per person.

founders.name: Lavika Aggarwal
founders.background_notes: Six years in compliance and risk at Capital One and co-owner of two patents per the YC page.

founders.name: Jagveer Gandhi
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by the Entrackr and DT Next coverage; background not found.

exit.reason: Reported by Entrackr and DT Next, not stated by the company in a source opened: an RBI directive barred UPI in co-branding arrangements, and Akudo was out of cash after failing to raise.

competitors.name: FamPay
competitors.what: Teen focused payments app and card in India, also YC backed
competitors.funding_then: US$38M Series A in June 2021 led by Elevation Capital with Sequoia Capital India; US$4.7M seed in March 2020

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a regulated card and UPI product on top of a licensed PPI issuer and a card processing partner needs integrations and compliance work but not new technology.

defensibility.rationale: The product depended on a partner's PPI licence rather than its own, and FamPay and other rivals offered near identical teen cards.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer emerged. Regulation, not incumbents, ended UPI based teen cards in mid 2023.

market_need_then: Reports in 2021 said the segment of teens under 18 was largely unserved and investors backed several teen fintechs. Akudo reported over 100,000 registered customers and over 25,000 cards issued at its seed announcement, per Entrackr.

branding.domain_note: Used akudo.in, an Indian domain, not a .com.

identity.visual_style: Described as sleek and personalized, aimed at teens
identity.voice_and_tone: Gamified and youth oriented, with the learning first banking pitch

branding.brand_signature: Learning first banking positioning and the Akudo squad Instagram community
branding.community_and_virality: An Instagram account named akudo_squad is linked from the YC page; no engagement evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly invented name and a clear teen positioning with press coverage at funding and shutdown, but no sourced evidence of virality or community pull.

outcome_analysis: Akudo raised a US$4.2M seed in September 2021 and grew to over 100,000 registered users. In June 2023 an RBI directive stopped UPI use in co-branded arrangements with issuers that lacked their own PPI licence, which hit Akudo along with FamPay and others. Reports in September 2023 say it was out of cash after failed fundraising, stopped onboarding and was winding down, and the wallet was to close on December 31, 2023.
notes: Seed amount and lead investors are stated by Inc42, Entrackr and DT Next. The pre-seed is listed on the YC page citing YourStory, with no amount. The akudo.in site returned HTTP 503 on fetch. The shutdown reason is press reporting citing sources; the company comment was not found. YourStory page returned 403 so the founders' education claim comes from YC page plus a search snippet from Inc42. Junio is a rival seen in search but no dated source URL was opened, so it is not listed. Audit fix: a 3.5M seed dated 2020-09 is listed only by BounceWatch (investors Amino Capital and Asymmetry Ventures); ZoomInfo and StartupIntros show only the 2021 seed, so this 2020 round is unverified and may be a data error. It is recorded flagged as single source.
